purpose: Pasireotide is used to treat Cushing's disease, a condition where your body makes too much of a stress hormone called cortisol. It is also used for a type of tumor called acromegaly, where your body makes too much growth hormone. This medicine helps bring those hormone levels back down to a safer range.
how_it_works: Your body has natural chemical messengers that help control hormone production. Pasireotide works by mimicking one of those messengers, called somatostatin, and attaching to special receptors in your body. This signals your body to slow down the production of cortisol or growth hormone, helping keep those levels under control.
common_side_effects: High blood sugar or diabetes is very common with this medicine, so your blood sugar will be checked regularly. You may also notice diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, or loose stools. Other common effects include feeling tired, headache, dizziness, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or pain.
warnings: This medication commonly causes high blood sugar, and some people may develop diabetes while taking it, so close monitoring is very important. It can also affect your heart rhythm, especially something called a prolonged QT interval, which is why your doctor will check your heart with an EKG. Tell your doctor right away if you notice a fast or irregular heartbeat, severe stomach pain, or yellowing of your skin or eyes, as it can also affect your liver and gallbladder.
typical_dosing: Signifor comes as a shot you give yourself under the skin twice a day. Signifor LAR is a longer-acting version given as an injection into the muscle by your healthcare provider once a month. Your doctor will start you on a dose that fits your condition and adjust it based on how well it is working and how you are tolerating it.
